info.title: AI Podcast Engine
info.summary: Create shows, generate grounded episodes and fetch their audio, notes and feeds.
info.description:
Turns web pages into podcast episodes: a scripted conversation between two AI hosts, grounded in
the pages' content, with every factual claim tied to the passage it comes from.

A **show** holds a topic, a speaking style and the pages to draw on. Each **episode** of a show is
generated in the background. The pages are fetched and split into sections, the passages that fit
the topic are selected, and a script is written in which each claim cites its passage. The script is
fact-checked and rewritten if a claim is not supported, then voiced, mixed into a single audio file
and published with show notes and an RSS feed.

A new episode of an existing show is a refresh: only the segments whose source sections changed
are regenerated, and nothing is regenerated if no source changed. Every episode is labelled as
AI-generated in its audio, show notes and feed.

get.description:
Start here. Lists every resource of the API with its URI or URI template, the methods it
allows, the formats it returns and accepts, whether it supports byte ranges or paging, and a
link to its documentation. Also says how authentication works (at present: it is not
required), where the liveness and readiness checks are, and the conventions every endpoint
follows.

The format is a JSON home document (draft-nottingham-json-home). Ask for
`application/json-home` to get that media type; otherwise it is served as `application/json`.

post.description:
Create an account. The very first account needs no token and becomes the admin. After that
an admin (sending their token) can create accounts as `creator` or `admin`; and when sign-up
is open (`SIGNUP_OPEN`), anyone can create their own account, always as a `creator`.

401.description: Accounts exist, sign-up is closed and no admin token was sent

429.description: Too many sign-ups from this address; wait and try again

403.description: The token is not an admin's

409.description: An account with this email already exists

post.description:
Exchange an email and password for a login token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer
<token>` on every other request. It lasts six months, until `POST /auth/logout`, or until the
account is disabled. Each login creates a new token; earlier ones keep working.

After five failed attempts within 15 minutes, the account is locked for 15 minutes (a password
reset unlocks it). The answer stays "wrong email or password" during the lock, so it does not
reveal which accounts exist. Many failures from one address get 429 with `Retry-After`.

200.description: A login token, valid for six months

401.description: Wrong email or password (also while the account is temporarily locked)

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this address; see `Retry-After`

post.description:
Sign in from a browser. The login token goes into the `pe_session` cookie (HttpOnly,
SameSite=Strict, six months), which page scripts cannot read, and the `pe_csrf` cookie holds
a CSRF token. Requests that change something must send it back in the `X-CSRF-Token` header.
The same limits as `POST /auth/login` apply. Scripts should use that endpoint or an API key.

200.description: The account; the login token is set as a cookie, not returned

401.description: Wrong email or password (also while the account is temporarily locked)

429.description: Too many failed attempts from this address; see `Retry-After`

delete.description:
Revoke the browser's login token and clear its cookies. If the token no longer works,
the cookies are still cleared, so a stale sign-in can always be ended.

204.description: Signed out; both cookies are cleared

403.description: The CSRF token is missing or wrong

get.description:
True until the first account exists. That account is created without signing in, with
`POST /auth/register`, and becomes the admin.

200.description: Whether the first account can still be created

post.description:
Email a single-use reset link, valid for 30 minutes, if an account has this address. The
answer is the same either way, and the email is sent after the response, so neither reveals
whether the account exists. At most three links per account per hour.

202.description: The same answer whether or not the account exists

429.description: Too many attempts from this address; see `Retry-After`

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset link
post.description:
Choose a new password with the token from the reset link. The link works once. Every login
token and API key of the account stops working, any lock on it is lifted, and a notice is
emailed. You are not signed in: log in with the new password.

204.description: The password is changed; sign in with it

422.description: The link is invalid, used or expired, or the password is too short

429.description: Too many attempts from this address; see `Retry-After`

get.description:
The finished episode audio, the same file the RSS feed points to.

Supports HTTP range requests, so it plays and seeks in a browser `<audio>` element and in
podcast apps. The AI-generated disclosure is the first thing spoken. Available once the
assemble stage has run; 404 before then.

The show's podcast feed, for podcast apps. Each item's enclosure is the episode's

404.description: No episode of this show has been published yet

Create a show, owned by you: its topic, style, hosts and the web pages its episodes are

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

post.description:
Create an episode and start generating it in the background. Returns at once, with the
episode `queued`; its status shows progress.

For a show that already has a published episode, this is a refresh: only segments whose
sources changed are re-scripted and re-voiced, and if no source changed the episode ends as
`unchanged`.

202.description: The new episode, `queued`; poll it for progress

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

503.description: Job queue unavailable; the episode is marked `failed`

200.description: A page of episodes, newest first

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

get.description:
Watch an episode being made, live: an event whenever its status or stage changes, until
nothing is running (published, held for review, unchanged, cancelled or failed). Browsers
connect with `EventSource`, which sends the sign-in cookie and reconnects by itself.

200.description: Server-sent events. `episode` carries the status, stage, step (of 8), error and rewrite count, sent whenever they change. `gone` means the episode was deleted. Comment lines keep the connection alive.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

get.description:
The script by segment. Each factual claim lists the passages it cites and the
fact-check verdict, so it can be reviewed before or after voicing. Empty until the
script stage has run.

200.description: Segments and lines, with each claim's citations and verdict

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

patch.description:
Replace the lines of one or more segments of an episode that is waiting for review.

A line with `chunk_ids` is a claim citing those passages (they must come from the show's
sources); a line without is framing. The script is fact-checked again. If it passes it goes
on to voicing (or waits for approval, if the show reviews before voicing); if it fails it
comes back for review. An edited script is never rewritten automatically.

200.description: The episode, queued for the fact-check again

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

503.description: Job queue unavailable; the edit is saved and the episode stays in review

409.description: The episode is not waiting for review

422.description: An unknown segment, speaker or passage

post.description:
Release an episode that is waiting for review to voicing, with its script as it is. This
includes a script the fact-check held back for unsupported claims: the reviewer decides, and
the verdicts stay on record.

200.description: The episode, queued for voicing

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

503.description: Job queue unavailable; the episode stays in review

409.description: The episode is not waiting for review

post.description:

200.description: The episode, queued at the stage it stopped at

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token

409.description: The episode has not failed or been cancelled

post.description:
Stop an episode that is queued, being generated or waiting for review. A stage that is
already running finishes, but no further stage runs. It can be resumed with a retry.

200.description: The episode, `cancelled`

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked token
